name: Provider Data Mis-match — ANL.1 lab filed thru wrong state
description: Ten steps: identify the ANL event, confirm the place of service is 81 and the provider is an independent laboratory, note the referring provider's Ancillary details and NPI, confirm the NPI against the claim image, search the provider database by NPI, find no match, and deny with PX_RANLAB.

steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab.
steps.hint: Click the 'Event Resolution' tab. The Active Edit panel shows PX_ANL — 'LAB FILED THRU WRONG STATE'. The All Edits list below shows it among the claim's other events.
steps.name: Identify the ANL event
steps.description: Open the Event Resolution tab and look through the claim's edits for an ANL event. The ANL event means a laboratory claim may have been filed through the wrong state: it should have been filed with the plan where the specimen was drawn, which is decided by where the REFERRING provider is located, and the referring provider is identified only by an NPI. Nothing on this tab tells you where that provider is. PX_ANL is present here, so work through the claim and establish it.

steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Claim Lines tab.
steps.hint: Claim Lines tab → Line 1 → POS. It reads 81, which is Independent Laboratory.
steps.checklistItem: Verify the Place of Service is 81
steps.name: Verify the Place of Service is 81
steps.description: Before the wrong-state rule is worth applying, establish that this really is a laboratory claim. Open the Claim Lines tab and read the POS field on the claim line. It reads 81 — Independent Laboratory — so the place of service is consistent with a lab claim and the rule is in scope. This is the first of two checks; the second is the provider's own specialty.

steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Provider Information tab.
steps.hint: Provider Info tab → Rendering section → Speciality description. It reads L02 - INDEPENDENT LABORATORY.
steps.checklistItem: Verify the provider specialty is Independent Laboratory
steps.name: Verify the provider specialty is Independent Laboratory
steps.description: Now the second check: the provider's own specialty. On the Provider Information tab, the Rendering section's Speciality description reads L02 - INDEPENDENT LABORATORY. The place of service and the specialty agree, so this is an independent laboratory claim and the ANL rule applies to it.

steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Claim Data → Details sub-tab.
steps.hint: Claim Data tab → Details sub-tab → Ancillary Provider. Type R, ZIP 12345, State NH.
steps.checklistItem: Note the referring provider's Ancillary details
steps.name: Note the referring provider's Ancillary details
steps.description: Open the Claim Data tab and its Details sub-tab, and find the Ancillary Provider section. Type reads R, which marks these as the REFERRING physician's details. The ZIP reads 12345 and the State reads NH. Note them, but do not treat them as the answer: this is where the claim CLAIMS the referring provider is, and whether that is right is exactly what the ANL event puts in question.

steps.completionTriggerNote: A deliberate return to the Provider Information tab, which step 3 already opened for the specialty. The trainee must go back to it while this step is active.
steps.hint: Provider Info tab → Referring section → NPI. It reads 12345678910.
steps.name: Note the referring provider NPI
steps.description: Go back to the Provider Information tab, this time for the Referring section. The NPI field reads 12345678910. This is the only identifier the claim carries for the referring provider, and everything that follows depends on it.

steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Claim Image tab.
steps.hint: Claim Image tab → Claim Image — Provider Information → Referring → field 17b. NPI. It reads 12345678910, the same as the claim record.
steps.checklistItem: Compare the NPI against the claim image
steps.name: Compare the NPI against the claim image
steps.description: The claim record is a keyed-in copy of the form the provider submitted, so check the NPI against the form itself. Open the Claim Image tab, find the Claim Image — Provider Information block, and read field 17b (NPI) in the Referring section. It reads 12345678910 — the same value you noted on the claim record. The NPI is present and correctly keyed, so there is nothing to re-key, and the question becomes who that NPI belongs to and where they are.

steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Search → Provider sub-tab. Opening it cannot complete the search step that follows — that one is graded on the Search press.
steps.hint: Search tab → Provider sub-tab. The Search Provider form opens with every filter box empty.
steps.name: Open the provider search
steps.description: No claim screen says where the referring provider is, so look them up. Open the Search tab and its Provider sub-tab. The Search Provider form opens empty, with the filter options blank — you are going to determine whether the referring provider exists in our database as an Our State provider.

steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Search press passes the action's guard: the NPI box must hold 12345678910, Source system must be SPS, and no other filter box may carry a value. The From and Through dates may be filled or left empty either way.
steps.hint: Enter 12345678910 in the NPI box, leave Source system on SPS and the other boxes empty, and click Search. The result reads 'No matching records found with the given search criteria'.
steps.checklistItem: Search by NPI and check the NPI Registry
steps.name: Search by NPI and check the NPI Registry
steps.description: Type the referring provider's NPI, 12345678910, into the NPI box and click Search. Leave Source system on SPS and every other filter box empty; the From and Through dates may be filled or left blank. The search returns no matching records with the given search criteria, so the referring provider is not in our database. The next step in the live system would be the NPPES NPI Registry at https://nppes.cms.hhs.gov/NPPESRegistry/NPIRegistrySearch.do?subAction=reset&searchType=ind — enter the NPI in the NPI Number field, click Search and review the provider details and address. In this application the NPI Registry is not accessed, and no matching record is found there either. The correct address cannot be determined, so the claim is rejected.

steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee submits the Deny panel with reject code PX_RANLAB.
steps.hint: Action menu → Deny claim → reject code PX_RANLAB → Submit.
steps.checklistItem: Deny the claim using Reject code PX_RANLAB
steps.name: Deny the claim using Reject code PX_RANLAB
steps.description: The correct address for the referring provider cannot be determined, so the claim cannot be routed to the plan where the specimen was drawn. Open the Action menu, select Deny claim, enter reject code PX_RANLAB and click Submit.

steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee submits Deny from the header Decision dropdown.
steps.name: Submit Deny decision
steps.description: Record the outcome on the claim. In the Decision section of the header, select Deny from the dropdown and click Submit.
